newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco winter-grade unleaded eases in Chicago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco winter-grade unleaded eases in Chicago.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent winter-grade unleaded gasoline prices eased on Thursday on weakening differentials, traders said.
Traders had a more difficult time pegging summer-grade unleaded differentials during a seasonal changeover that takes effect at the end of April.
"The market is going to bounce around a little bit this month," one trader said earlier in the day of volatile trade expected in the weeks leading up to the end-of-the-month changeover.
Chicago winter-grade unleaded gasoline eased to 9.25/9.0 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, with summer-grade unleaded between four and six cents firmer, traders said.
Group Three unleaded remained 2.50/2.75 cents a gallon under the print for prompt barrels, with later deliveries steady at 0.25 cent a gallon weaker.
Diesel differentials were largely unchanged on the day, leaving prices to track modestly higher NYMEX April heating oil futures.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was bid 3.75 cents a gallon over April NYMEX heating oil for prompt deliveries and 3.50 cents a gallon over the print for later deliveries, unchanged on the day.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was talked 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 4.50/4.75 cents over the print for later deliveries, traders said.
